answer: Clock-drift fingerprinting mitigates Sybil attacks by measuring microscopic timing imperfections in a host's quartz oscillator. Because virtual instances on shared hardware exhibit identical skew, an attacker must procure physically separate timing crystals per identity. This establishes an operational haven against mass virtualized bots. A key limitation is that thermal shifts make timing profiles far less stable than marble, generating drift noise that misclassifies honest agents.
